methodological_rigor.justification: The study is described as a 'prospective, double-blind' single-center trial of 210 consecutive PTC patients with preoperative CTC counts measured by the TUMORFISHER platform, but there is an internal inconsistency: the Discussion also labels the study as 'single-center, retrospective.' No control cohort (benign thyroid disease or healthy controls) is included beyond spike-in experiments; risk stratification references are only postoperative pathology. Cutoffs (≥1, ≥2 CTCs) appear data-derived rather than pre-specified, with no cross-validation or held-out test set and no multiplicity correction across the many ROC analyses. The PTMC PFS analysis has only two recurrence events driving an extremely wide HR 95% CI (0.002–0.726), and no multivariable adjustment for established risk factors is reported.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preoperative risk stratification in PTC—especially PTMC where active surveillance is debated—is clinically important, and the proposed dual-threshold CTC test is positioned as actionable. However, the specificity of the test and platform, the single-center design, and the small numbers in subgroups (19 high-risk PTMC, 8 metastatic) mean findings are hypothesis-generating rather than practice-changing. As a single-center prospective cohort/diagnostic study, Oxford LoE maps best to 2b (individual cohort study) rather than 1b.

reporting_quality.justification: As a diagnostic accuracy study, STARD is the applicable standard. Many items are partially addressed (inclusion criteria, index test description, reference standard defined as postoperative pathology/ATA/LNM-CG, AUC with sensitivity/specificity/PPV/NPV), but key STARD items are missing or weak: no STARD flow diagram, no pre-specified cutoffs (thresholds are data-derived from the same cohort), no external or split-sample validation, and inconsistent descriptors of study design (prospective vs. retrospective). No data availability statement, accession number, or code repository is referenced.

novelty_literature.justification: CTC detection in thyroid cancer is not a new concept—the paper itself cites Ringel 1998, Yu 2024, Lin 2018, and Innaro 2022, as well as a published meta-analysis (Liang 2022). The novelty lies in applying the peptide-functionalized TUMORFISHER platform specifically to preoperative risk stratification in PTC/PTMC with a dual-threshold (rule-in/rule-out) decision model and in testing association with PFS at 44-month follow-up. This is a meaningful extension in one direction rather than a first-in-class discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is organized in a conventional IMRaD structure with dedicated figures for assay validation, ROC analyses, PTMC subgroup, and Kaplan–Meier PFS. Writing is generally clear but includes promotional phrasing ('paradigm-shifting,' 'precision medicine,' 'transform PTC management') that weakens scientific tone, and Methods/Discussion contain the prospective vs. retrospective inconsistency. Figure legends are detailed, but some results are repeated across sections, and the anecdotal single-patient DSV-PTC narrative in the Discussion is out of place for a diagnostic accuracy study.

key_strengths: Addresses a real clinical problem (preoperative risk stratification of PTC/PTMC) with a noninvasive liquid biopsy approach
Reasonable cohort size (n=210) for a single-center thyroid CTC study with 44-month median follow-up and pre-specified analytic validation of EpCAM-based capture in cell lines
Dual-threshold decision framework (rule-out ≥1 CTC, rule-in ≥2 CTC) offers clinically interpretable cutoffs with reported sensitivity/specificity/PPV/NPV and AUCs (0.81–0.99)
key_concerns: Internal inconsistency between 'prospective, double-blind' design in Methods and 'single-center, retrospective' framing in Discussion undermines trust in study design
Cutoffs derived and tested on the same cohort without external validation, split-sample, or cross-validation, and no multiplicity correction across numerous ROC analyses
PFS analysis in PTMC rests on few events (recurrence 5.71%, 2/35) producing very wide HR 95% CI (0.002–0.726) that is fragile and not adjusted for established clinicopathologic risk factors
Very small subgroups (8 patients with distant metastasis, 19 high-risk PTMC) underpin some of the strongest claims
No data/code availability statement; reporting deviates materially from STARD checklist items including flow diagram and pre-specified thresholds
Promotional language ('paradigm-shifting,' 'transform PTC management') inconsistent with single-center level of evidence
chief_reviewer.rationale: The topic is clinically important and the cohort size adequate for a preliminary study, but methodological and reporting weaknesses—particularly the prospective/retrospective inconsistency, absence of external validation, and fragile PFS evidence—limit tier-3 acceptability to major revisions.
